title: Add `orch abort <run>` CLI command

checks.name: usage
checks.cmd: cd orchestrator && node src/cli.ts abort; test $? -ne 0

checks.name: help
checks.cmd: cd orchestrator && node src/cli.ts | grep -q 'orch abort <run>'

brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24 (no build), folder orchestrator/. Read orchestrator/src/cli.ts (the HELP string and the `case "resume":` block) and `abort(id: string)` in orchestrator/src/engine.ts (returns "stopping" | "aborted" | "done", throws if another process runs it). Do not change engine.ts.
1. In the HELP string, right after the two `orch resume` lines, add: `  orch abort <run>                       stop a run (a waiting run at once); its branches stay`, aligned like the other lines.
2. Add `case "abort": {` next to `case "resume"`: if `!args[0]` throw `new Error("usage: orch abort <run>")`; otherwise `console.log(`${args[0]}: ${engine.abort(args[0])}`)`; then `break;`.
Done when the three checks pass. Change only orchestrator/src/cli.ts.

title: Plan prompt: read-only requests become research tasks, not docs
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24, folder orchestrator/. Read `planPrompt` in orchestrator/src/prompts.ts, the RULES array. Bug from a real run: the senior turned "explain X (research only)" into a `docs` task, which edits files.
1. In the RULES array, directly after the line starting "- files: exact repo-relative paths", add one string: "- When the request only asks to explain, investigate, analyse or answer a question (nothing should change), use category research with files [] and no checks; the report is the answer. Use docs only when the request asks to write or change documentation files."
Done when the checks pass. Change nothing else; keep the 'ORCH:senior.plan' marker and the JSON example unchanged.
